name: activity-announcer
title: Activity announcer
purpose: The one status region of a view that tells a screen reader what an agent's run is doing: always in the page, never drawn, and written to only when the run starts, needs approval, finishes, stops or fails.
whenToUse: Once in every view that shows an agent working: beside the transcript, in the page from the first render.
Together with a transcript that is a named log with aria-live off, so the transcript itself never speaks.
whenNotToUse: For a message the reader also needs to see. Show it in the view, as an alert, a toast or a row, and write the same words here only if that element is not itself announced.
For how many approvals wait across the app. The pending tray has its own region.
More than once in a view. Two regions talk over each other.
accessibility: Use one p with the class gw-activity-announcer and role="status". It is in the page from the first render and stays there, empty, for as long as the view does. A region added at the moment it is needed is often not announced, and one hidden with the hidden attribute or display none never is.

The transcript is a div with role="log", aria-live="off" and an aria-label that names it, around the ol of rows. The role says what the region is, the name lets the reader find it, and aria-live="off" stops it speaking each row and each word as it lands.

Write one short sentence into the region at each of five moments, and at no other. Started: Claude Code started working. Needs approval: Approval needed: run npm install. Finished: Claude Code finished: ran 4 commands, edited 2 files. Stopped: Stopped. The work so far is kept. Failed: A step failed: npm test exited with code 1. The words are the app's own.
The finished sentence carries the counts for the whole turn, in the same plain words as a step group's summary. That one sentence stands in for every step that was not announced.

Never announce a time that counts up, a word or a token of text as it arrives, a row that is added, or each step of a run of steps that needed no approval. Never put aria-live on the growing text of a message.

To say the same sentence twice in a row, empty the region and write the sentence again a moment later. Leave a second or two between sentences, and when several things happen at once say the one the reader must act on.
A request for approval is announced and nothing more: focus stays where the reader is, which is usually the composer. They reach the request from the now-doing line's link or by reading the log.
For a failure that stops the whole run and needs the reader now, a visible error row or alert with role="alert" may speak for itself. Then leave this region alone for that moment.
The stylesheet only keeps the region out of sight. The component needs no script of its own: the app sets the text.
